description: Guide a student to implement a Simple Moving Average (SMA) trend-following strategy as a LEAN C# algorithm on a single crypto future (BTCUSDT). The student must subscribe to one symbol, create an SMA indicator, implement a price-vs-SMA entry/exit rule, handle warm-up correctly, and produce a trade log. This is the simplest possible LEAN strategy — the 'hello world' of algorithmic trading on QuantConnect.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I have access to a trading engine called LEAN with Bitcoin futures data. I want to test a simple moving average strategy — buy when the price is above the average, sell when it's below. I've never written C# before. Where do I start?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need to implement a basic SMA trend filter on LEAN for BTCUSDT daily bars. I know the concept but I've never used the QuantConnect API. How do I set up the algorithm, register the indicator, and manage positions?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm bootstrapping a LEAN environment for the first time. I want to start with the simplest possible strategy — SMA(20) on BTCUSDT daily — to validate my setup end-to-end before scaling to multi-symbol. What's the minimal correct implementation?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Student produces a working LEAN C# algorithm that (1) subscribes to BTCUSDT daily futures via AddCryptoFuture, (2) creates an SMA(20) indicator, (3) goes long when price > SMA and flattens when price < SMA, (4) handles warm-up correctly with SetWarmUp, (5) runs to completion, and (6) produces a trade log with entry/exit records.
required_capabilities: Write a LEAN C# algorithm inheriting QCAlgorithm
Subscribe to a single crypto future with AddCryptoFuture
Create and use an SMA indicator with correct resolution
Implement price-vs-SMA entry/exit logic in OnData
Handle warm-up period with SetWarmUp and IsWarmingUp guard
Run the backtest and interpret the results
